subject: science
sourceNote: Converted from user-provided Grade 10 Science MCQ Part 1 DOCX. Answer options were rebalanced for better quiz experience.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What are the main features of organisms under kingdom plantae?
options: Eukaryotic cell, cell with cell wall, heterotrophs
Eukaryotic cell, cell without cell wall, heterotrophs
Eukaryotic cell, cell with cell wall, saprotrophs
Eukaryotic cell, cell with cell wall, autotrophs
questions.explanation: Plantae have eukaryotic cells, cell wall and make food. Autotroph means they can make their own food.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is Cycas kept in gymnosperm?
options: Bears cones instead of flowers, seeds are naked without fruit
Bears cones instead of flowers, seeds are enclosed in fruit
questions.explanation: Cycas has cones and naked seeds. Naked seeds are not covered by fruit.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Two animals are shown in the textbook figure. They belong to the same kingdom. What is the reason?
options: Multicellular and have various organ systems
questions.explanation: Animals are multicellular and depend on others for food. This puts them in the same kingdom Animalia.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Based on evolution, which of the following groups of organisms are closely related?
questions.explanation: These groups are closer in body plan and evolution. So they are shown as closely related.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the main reason for classifying whales in the class Mammalia?
options: Vertebral column is found in the body
Gives birth and suckles milk to young ones
questions.explanation: Whales give birth and feed milk to young ones. These are main features of mammals.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why are club mosses more advanced than mosses?
options: Xylem and phloem tissue are found in clubmoss
questions.explanation: Club moss has xylem and phloem. These tissues make it more advanced than moss.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: To which kingdom do organisms having cell walls belong?
questions.explanation: Monera, fungi and plantae have cell walls. Animalia does not have a cell wall.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: To which class do egg-laying animals with a four-chambered heart and body covered with feather belong?
questions.explanation: Aves means birds. Birds lay eggs, have feathers and a four-chambered heart.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which of the following groups of plants belongs to angiosperm?
questions.explanation: Paddy, banana and mango are flowering plants. Their seeds are inside fruits, so they are angiosperms.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which division do the plants having vascular tissue belong to?
questions.explanation: Tracheophyta plants have vascular tissues. Xylem and phloem carry water and food.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: According to the five kingdom system in the chapter, which kingdom contains organisms with prokaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Monera has prokaryotic cells. Prokaryotic cells do not have a true nucleus.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which kingdom includes unicellular eukaryotic organisms in the chart?
questions.explanation: Protista includes unicellular eukaryotes. Eukaryotic cells have a true nucleus.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What feature separates animals from many other kingdoms in the five-kingdom chart?
questions.explanation: Animal cells do not have cell walls. This separates animals from plants and fungi.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is fern called an autotroph in the introductory discussion?
options: Because it has no cell wall
questions.explanation: Fern has chlorophyll. Chlorophyll helps it make its own food.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which group of plants is classified as algae in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Spirogyra, Volvox and Fucus are algae. Algae are simple plants with chlorophyll.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which statement is true for algae according to the chapter?
options: They are autotrophs due to chlorophyll
questions.explanation: Algae have chlorophyll and make food. So they are autotrophs.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the plant cell wall of algae made of?
questions.explanation: Algae cell wall is made of cellulose. Cellulose gives support to plant cells.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which group includes Marchantia, moss and Riccia?
questions.explanation: Marchantia, moss and Riccia are bryophytes. Bryophytes are simple non-vascular plants.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why do plants under Bryophyta need water for fertilization?
options: They make fruits only in water
Their male gamete swims through water to reach the female gamete
They have xylem vessels only in water
questions.explanation: Male gametes need water to swim to female gametes. So bryophytes need water for fertilization.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which feature is absent in bryophytes according to the chapter?
questions.explanation: Bryophytes do not have vascular tissue. That means they lack xylem and phloem.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which plant division has xylem and phloem as vascular tissues?
questions.explanation: Tracheophyta has xylem and phloem. These tissues transport water and food.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Into which three sub-divisions is Tracheophyta divided in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Tracheophyta is divided into these three groups. They are based on seeds and plant body features.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which feature is found in pteridophytes like fern and horsetail?
options: They have no seeds but are differentiated into root, stem and leaf
questions.explanation: Pteridophytes have root, stem and leaf. But they do not produce seeds.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Where are sori found in pteridophytes according to the chapter?
options: On the lower surface of leaves
questions.explanation: Sori are found on the lower side of leaves. They are small spore-producing structures.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What do sori produce in fern-like plants?
questions.explanation: Sori produce spores. Spores help fern-like plants reproduce.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What do gymnosperms bear instead of flowers?
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms bear cones. They do not bear true flowers.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why are gymnosperm seeds called naked?
options: They are not enclosed in fruit
questions.explanation: Gymnosperm seeds are not inside fruit. So they are called naked seeds.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which plants are listed as gymnosperms in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Cycas, Pinus and Juniper are gymnosperms. They have cones and naked seeds.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which plants are described as real flowering plants?
questions.explanation: Angiosperms are real flowering plants. They produce flowers and fruits.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What happens to angiosperm seeds?
options: They are produced by spores only
They are kept in cones only
questions.explanation: Angiosperm seeds are inside fruit. Fruit protects the seeds.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which is a characteristic of monocotyledonous plants?
questions.explanation: Monocot leaves usually have parallel veins. So parallel venation is a monocot feature.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which is a characteristic of dicotyledonous plants?
questions.explanation: Dicot plants usually have tap roots. Tap root is a main feature of dicots.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How are vascular bundles arranged in dicot stems according to the chapter?
questions.explanation: In dicot stems, vascular bundles form a ring. This is different from scattered bundles in monocots.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which feature belongs to kingdom Animalia?
options: Eukaryotic cells without cell wall and heterotrophic nutrition
questions.explanation: Animals have eukaryotic cells without cell wall. They get food from other organisms.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How are animals without vertebral column called?
questions.explanation: Animals without backbone are invertebrates. Vertebrates have a backbone.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which phylum contains sponges such as Spongilla, Sycon and Euspongia?
questions.explanation: Sponges belong to Porifera. Spongilla, Sycon and Euspongia are examples.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which is a key feature of Porifera?
options: Water enters through ostia and exits through osculum
questions.explanation: Porifera body has pores called ostia. Water enters through ostia and leaves through osculum.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which phylum has tentacles and a hollow cavity called coelenteron?
questions.explanation: Coelenterata have tentacles and coelenteron. Coelenteron is a hollow body cavity.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which phylum includes flatworms such as tapeworm and liver fluke?
questions.explanation: Tapeworm and liver fluke are flatworms. Flatworms belong to Platyhelminthes.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which phylum includes roundworm, hookworm and pinworm?
questions.explanation: Roundworm, hookworm and pinworm are roundworms. They belong to Nemathelminthes.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which feature best identifies Annelida?
questions.explanation: Annelids have long segmented bodies. Earthworm is a common example.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why are arthropods placed in phylum Arthropoda?
options: They have jointed legs and a chitinous exoskeleton
questions.explanation: Arthropods have jointed legs and a hard outer covering. This outer covering is made of chitin.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which phylum contains soft-bodied animals with mantle and muscular feet?
questions.explanation: Mollusca animals have soft bodies. They often have mantle and muscular foot.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which phylum includes animals with spiny skin and tube feet?
questions.explanation: Echinoderms have spiny skin and tube feet. Starfish is a common example.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which feature is common in phylum Chordata according to the chapter?
options: Notochord at some stage of life
questions.explanation: Chordates have a notochord at some stage. This is their important common feature.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which class has animals with gills, fins and a two-chambered heart?
questions.explanation: Pisces are fishes. They have gills, fins and a two-chambered heart.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which class includes animals whose young ones are tadpoles that respire through gills?
questions.explanation: Amphibian young ones are tadpoles. Tadpoles breathe through gills.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which class has body covered with feathers and hollow pneumatic bones?
questions.explanation: Aves are birds. Birds have feathers and hollow bones.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which class is identified by hair, mammary glands and viviparous birth?
questions.explanation: Mammals have hair and mammary glands. They usually give birth to young ones.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What relationship does the chapter show between classification and evolution?
options: Classification shows similarities and common ancestry among organisms
Classification proves organisms do not change
Evolution removes the need for classification
Only animals evolve but plants do not
questions.explanation: Classification shows similarities among organisms. Similar organisms may have common ancestors.
